mainTopic: The suffering, death, burial and greatness of רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון
overview: This amud is one long aggadic story about רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, not a legal debate. Out of fear that he had ruled wrongly, he took suffering upon himself. He welcomed his pains every night and sent them away every morning so he would not lose Torah learning. His wife nursed him but kept him out of the בית מדרש. When she learned the pains were self-inflicted, she left him. Sixty sailors then came to care for him, and he returned to the בית מדרש, where Heaven confirmed his rulings on blood samples. After his death his body lay in his attic for many years without decaying, until the רבנן finally buried him beside his father, רבי שמעון בן יוחאי. His widow turned down רבי's marriage proposal, and the גמרא tells how רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון was greater than רבי in Torah. The amud ends as רבי begins listing three humble people, starting with his father.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר takes suffering upon himself
steps.stepSummary: Even after the earlier sign, רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון did not trust himself, so he accepted יסורין. Every night sixty felt covers were spread under him, and every morning sixty basins of blood and pus were taken out from under him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even so, רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון did not rely on his own judgment, and he accepted suffering upon himself. At night they spread sixty felt covers under him, and in the morning they pulled sixty basins of blood and pus out from under him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the story of רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון and tells us he chose to accept suffering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'even so' tie back to the earlier part of the story, where he received a sign that he had not done wrong. He still worried he might have made a mistake, so he accepted יסורין as an atonement. The number sixty, which repeats all through this story, shows how extreme the suffering was.

keyTerms.meaning: He did not rely on his own judgment

phrases.english: And even so, he did not rely
Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon on his own judgment,
he accepted sufferings upon himself.

phrases.aramaic: בְּאוּרְתָּא הֲווֹ מָיְיכִי לֵיהּ שִׁיתִּין נַמְטֵי,
phrases.english: At night they would spread out sixty felt covers for him,
in the morning they would pull out from under him
sixty basins of blood and pus.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַאֲפִילּוּ הָכִי לָא סְמַךְ רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אַדַּעְתֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Picks the story of רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון back up from the earlier part of the daf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Out of humility and fear of having erred, רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון accepted severe suffering upon himself.

steps.title: His wife's daily care and her worry
steps.stepSummary: Each day his wife made him sixty kinds of fig relish, which healed him. She would not let him go to the בית מדרש, so that the רבנן would not push him too hard.
steps.simpleTranslation: The next day his wife would make him sixty kinds of relish, and he ate them and became healthy. His wife would not let him go out to the study hall, so that the Rabbis would not push him too hard.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא describes how his wife nursed him back to health each day and protected him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The pattern is a daily cycle: sick at night, healed by morning. His wife kept him home because she feared the strain of learning with the רבנן would wear him down after such suffering.

keyTerms.meaning: His wife (literally, 'the one of his house')
A relish or dish, made from figs
That they would press or strain him

phrases.english: The next day his wife would make for him
sixty kinds of relish
and he would eat them and become healthy.
And his wife would not let him
go out to the study hall
so that the Rabbis would not push him too hard.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story: after the night of suffering comes the morning of healing.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: His wife healed him daily with special food and kept him from overexertion in the בית מדרש.

steps.title: Inviting the pains at night, sending them away by morning
steps.stepSummary: Every evening he called his pains 'my brothers and friends' and invited them in. Every morning he told them to leave, because they kept him from learning Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the evening he would say to them: My brothers and my friends, come! In the morning he would say to them: Go away, because of the loss of Torah learning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows how he spoke to his own pains, welcoming them at night and dismissing them in the morning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He saw the suffering as a friend, since it brought atonement. But he would not let it cost him daytime learning, so he sent it away because of ביטול תורה. His love of suffering was limited by his greater love of Torah.

phrases.english: In the evening he would say to them:
phrases.notes: 'Them' means his pains. He is speaking to his sufferings as if they were people.

phrases.english: My brothers and my friends, come!
In the morning he would say to them:
Go away, because of the loss of Torah learning.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּאוּרְתָּא אֲמַר לְהוּ אַחַיי וְרֵעַי בּוֹאוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the nightly suffering and morning recovery worked from his side.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: He welcomed his sufferings at night and dismissed them in the morning so as not to lose Torah learning.

steps.title: His wife hears him and leaves
steps.stepSummary: One day his wife heard him inviting the pains. She complained that he was bringing them on himself and using up her father's money, and she left him and went back to her family's home.
steps.simpleTranslation: One day his wife heard him. She said to him: You are bringing them upon yourself! You have used up the money of my father's house. She rebelled and went to her family's home.
steps.whatsHappening: The story takes a turn: his wife finds out the suffering is self-inflicted and leaves him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now she believed she was treating an illness. Once she learned he was calling the pains himself, she felt her family's money was being wasted. Her leaving sets up the next scene, since now no one is caring for him.

keyTerms.meaning: You have used up the money

phrases.english: One day his wife heard him,

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַרָה לֵיהּ: אַתְּ קָא מַיְיתֵית לְהוּ עִילָּוָיךְ!
phrases.english: she said to him: You are bringing them upon yourself!
You have used up the money of my father's house.
She rebelled, and went to her family's home.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: His words to the pains in the last step are what his wife overhears here.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: His wife, upset that he invited his suffering at her family's expense, left him.

steps.title: Sixty sailors come to care for him
steps.stepSummary: Sixty sailors arrived and brought him sixty servants, each carrying sixty purses. They made him sixty kinds of relish, and he ate them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Those sixty sailors came up and arrived. They brought in for him sixty servants holding sixty purses, and they made him sixty kinds of relish, and he ate them.
steps.whatsHappening: Just when his wife has left, sixty sailors show up and take over his care, with even more wealth than before.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story shows that he was not abandoned. The same food his wife used to make, sixty kinds of relish, is now provided by the sailors, along with servants and money. The repeated number sixty links this scene to the earlier ones.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון accepted suffering out of fear of having erred, welcomed it at night and sent it away for the sake of Torah by day, and even when his wife left, he was cared for by others.

phrases.english: Those sixty sailors came up and arrived,
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets, 'sixty', is added in the corrected wording.

phrases.english: they brought in for him sixty servants
holding sixty purses,
and they made for him sixty kinds of relish
and he ate them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After his wife leaves, the sailors arrive and take her place in caring for him.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sixty sailors arrived with servants, money and food, and they cared for him.

steps.title: He tells his wife he is now richer, gets healthy, and returns to learning
steps.stepSummary: His wife sends their daughter to check on him. He answers that his wealth is now greater than her family's, quotes a פסוק about himself, and goes back to the בית מדרש.
steps.simpleTranslation: One day his wife told their daughter: 'Go see what your father is doing now.' The daughter came, and he told her: 'Go tell your mother that ours is greater than theirs.' He applied the פסוק to himself: 'She is like the merchant ships; she brings her bread from afar.' He ate, drank, became healthy, and went out to the בית מדרש.
steps.whatsHappening: The wife who left him sends their daughter to find out how he is doing. He sends back word that he is now richer than her family, and since nobody is holding him back anymore, he returns to the בית מדרש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 4 she complained that he was using up her father's money. Now the sailors' gift from Step 5 has made him richer than her family. With her gone, nothing stops him from going to the בית מדרש, which is exactly what she had prevented in Step 2.

keyTerms.meaning: He read [the פסוק] about himself, applied it to himself
The study hall, the בית מדרש

phrases.english: One day, she said to her daughter:
phrases.notes: "She" is his wife, who had gone back to her family's home.

phrases.english: Go, check on your father
what is he doing now?
She came, and he said to her:
Go, tell your mother:
Ours is greater than theirs.
phrases.notes: He means his wealth is now bigger than her father's family's.

phrases.english: He read about himself:
"She is like the merchant ships;
from afar she brings her bread."
phrases.notes: משלי 31:14

phrases.english: He ate and drank and became healthy
and went out to the study hall.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story right after the sailors bring him wealth.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Once he was wealthy and his wife no longer held him back, he became healthy and returned to the בית מדרש.

steps.title: His rulings on sixty blood samples are proven right by a sign
steps.stepSummary: He declares sixty blood samples טהור. The רבנן doubt that none was even questionable, so he asks for a sign. All the babies born are boys, and they are named after him.
steps.simpleTranslation: They brought him sixty kinds of blood, and he declared them all טהור. The רבנן murmured: 'Can you really believe that not even one of them was a ספק?' He told them: 'If the הלכה is like me, let all the babies be boys. If not, let one girl be among them.' All of them were boys, and they named them 'אלעזר' after him.
steps.whatsHappening: Back in the בית מדרש, he rules that sixty blood samples are טהור, meaning the women may be with their husbands. The רבנן are doubtful, and Heaven proves him right through a sign.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן's doubt is not about one ruling. It is that it seems impossible that all sixty were clear, with not even one ספק. His sign, all boys, shows Heaven agrees with his rulings, and naming the babies after him shows how the people saw it.

keyTerms.meaning: Kinds of blood: samples brought to check whether they make a woman טמאה

phrases.aramaic: אַיְיתוֹ לְקַמֵּיהּ שִׁיתִּין מִינֵי דְּמָא – טַהֲרִינְהוּ.
phrases.english: They brought sixty kinds of blood before him; he declared them pure.
The Rabbis were murmuring and saying:

phrases.aramaic: סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ לֵית בְּהוּ חַד סָפֵק?!
phrases.english: Can you imagine that there is not one doubtful case among them?!
He said to them: If [the halacha] is like me,
let all of them be males,
phrases.notes: He means all the babies these women will have.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם לָאו – תְּהֵא נְקֵבָה אַחַת בֵּינֵיהֶם.
phrases.english: and if not, let there be one female among them.
They were all males.
And they called them "Elazar" after him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows what happened once he returned to the בית מדרש.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: His lenient rulings on the blood samples were confirmed by Heaven: all sixty babies were boys.

steps.title: רבי criticizes the wife for keeping him from the בית מדרש
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי saying that this wicked woman prevented many children from being born in Israel.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: רבי said: How much having children did this wicked woman stop from Israel!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא where רבי comments on the story. He blames the wife for the children who were never born.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 7 showed that his rulings let couples be together and have children. All the years she kept him home (Step 2), those rulings never happened, so רבי says she held back many births.
steps.whatToRemember: The wife thought she was protecting him, but keeping a great פוסק out of the בית מדרש had a real cost: couples who could have been permitted to each other were not.

phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi said:
phrases.notes: "רבי" by itself means רבי יהודה הנשיא.

phrases.english: How much having children has she stopped,
this wicked woman, from Israel.
phrases.notes: He means the wife who kept him home, so his lenient rulings never reached people.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a lesson from Step 7 about the harm the wife caused earlier.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: By keeping him out of the בית מדרש, his wife caused fewer children to be born in Israel.

steps.title: Before dying, he asks to be laid in his attic
steps.stepSummary: As he is dying, he tells his wife the רבנן are angry at him and won't care for his body properly, so she should lay him in the attic and not be afraid.
steps.simpleTranslation: When he was dying, he said to his wife: 'I know the רבנן are angry at me and will not take care of me properly. Lay me in my attic, and don't be afraid of me.'
steps.whatsHappening: The story jumps to the end of his life. He gives his wife instructions about his body after he dies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He expects the רבנן will not give him a proper burial because they are upset with him. Instead of burial, he asks to be kept in his own attic, and tells his wife not to fear anything bad will happen to his body. This sets up the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: His soul was resting: he was dying

phrases.english: When he was dying,
he said to his wife:
I know that the Rabbis are angry at me,
and they will not take care of me properly.
phrases.notes: He means they won't handle his burial properly.

phrases.english: Lay me in my attic
and do not be afraid of me.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves the story forward to his death.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: He asked to be laid in his attic rather than buried, because he expected the רבנן would not care for him properly.

steps.title: Witness report: he lay in the attic for eighteen to twenty-two years
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמואל בר נחמני reports, through a chain of two women, that the wife kept his body in the attic for between eighteen and twenty-two years.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמואל בר נחמני said: The mother of רבי יונתן told me that the wife of רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון told her: 'For no less than eighteen and no more than twenty-two years, I kept him lying in the attic.'
steps.whatsHappening: An אמורא confirms that the wife did what he asked. He reports how long the body stayed in the attic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The report comes through a chain: the wife told רבי יונתן's mother, who told רבי שמואל בר נחמני. It shows his instruction in Step 9 was carried out for many years.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shmuel bar Naḥmani said:
The mother of Rabbi Yonatan told me

phrases.aramaic: דְּאִישְׁתַּעְיָא לַהּ דְּבֵיתְהוּ דְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן:
phrases.english: that the wife of Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon told her:
No less than eighteen
and no more than twenty-two years
I kept him lying in the attic.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Confirms that the instruction in Step 9 was carried out, and for how long.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: His wife kept his body in the attic for between eighteen and twenty-two years.

steps.title: The wife describes his body and the worm in his ear
steps.stepSummary: The wife reports that his body did not decay. She was upset to see a worm, but he came to her in a dream and explained it was for not protesting an insult to a Torah scholar.
steps.simpleTranslation: When I went up to the attic, I would check his hair. When a hair fell out, blood would come out. One day I saw a worm coming out of his ear and I became upset. He appeared to me in a dream and said: It is nothing. One day I heard a young Torah scholar being insulted, and I did not protest the way I should have.
steps.whatsHappening: The wife keeps describing what she saw in the attic. She learns in a dream that the one worm was a small punishment for a specific sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Blood coming out where a hair fell shows his body was still like a living body and did not rot. The worm looked like the start of decay, but he explains it was only a punishment. It came in his ear because he heard an insult to a תלמיד חכם and did not speak up.

phrases.english: When I would go up
phrases.notes: The wife is still speaking. She means going up to the attic where his body lay.

phrases.english: I would check his hair
when a hair would fall out from him
blood would come out
One day I saw a worm
coming out of his ear
I became very upset
He appeared to me in a dream and said to me:
It is nothing
One day I heard
a young Torah scholar being insulted
and I did not protest as I should have

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי הֲוָה סָלְיקָנָא מְעַיְּנָנָא לֵיהּ בְּמַזְיֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the wife's report about the years his body lay in the attic
steps.mimraCoreRuling: His body did not decay. The one worm was a punishment for failing to protest an insult to a תלמיד חכם.

steps.title: A voice from the attic judges court cases
steps.stepSummary: People with a court case would stand at the door and each tell his side. A voice from the attic would then announce who was liable and who was innocent.
steps.simpleTranslation: When two people came for a court case, they stood at the door. One said his side and the other said his side. A voice came out of his attic and said: So-and-so, you are liable. So-and-so, you are innocent.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells another wonder from those years. Even from the attic, רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון kept judging cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This adds that his greatness went beyond his body not decaying. He kept serving as a judge after his death, and people still came to his house for rulings.

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הֲווֹ אָתוּ בֵּי תְרֵי לְדִינָא,
phrases.english: When two people would come for a court case
they would stand at the door
one would say his side
and the other would say his side
a voice would come out of his attic and say:
So-and-so, you are liable
So-and-so, you are innocent

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי הֲווֹ אָתוּ בֵּי תְרֵי לְדִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another wonder from the period when his body lay in the attic
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even after his death he judged cases from his attic.

steps.title: A neighbor's insult reveals he was never buried
steps.stepSummary: During a fight, a neighbor cursed the wife to be like her husband who was never buried. The רבנן then said this could not go on.
steps.simpleTranslation: One day his wife was fighting with a neighbor. The neighbor said to her: May she be like her husband, who was not buried! The רבנן said: This much is certainly not proper.
steps.whatsHappening: The secret comes out through a neighbor's angry words. Now that the רבנן know, they decide that leaving him unburied is not right.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the wife had kept his body hidden in the attic. Once everyone knows, the רבנן say it is not proper to leave things this way, and this starts the process of burying him.

keyTerms.meaning: Proper conduct, the right way to act

phrases.english: One day was quarreling
his wife with a neighbor
She said to her:
phrases.notes: The neighbor is talking to the wife and cursing her, speaking about her as "she."

phrases.english: May she be like her husband, who was not given burial
The Rabbis said:

phrases.aramaic: כּוּלֵּי הַאי וַדַּאי לָאו אוֹרַח אַרְעָא.
phrases.english: This much is certainly not proper conduct

steps.triggerLanguage: יוֹמָא חַד הֲוָה קָא מִינַּצְיָא דְּבֵיתְהוּ בַּהֲדֵי שִׁבָבְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the wonders in the attic to how the matter became known
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Once his lack of burial became known, the רבנן said it was not proper to leave him unburied.

steps.title: Another version: his father asks in a dream for his son
steps.stepSummary: A second version says the רבנן found out because רבי שמעון בן יוחאי came to them in a dream and asked why they were not bringing his son to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: רבי שמעון בן יוחאי appeared to them in a dream. He said to them: I have one young bird among you, and you do not want to bring it to me?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different version of how the רבנן learned they needed to bury him: his father asked them in a dream.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version, a neighbor's insult revealed the secret. In this version his father רבי שמעון בן יוחאי asks for his son to be buried next to him. Both versions lead to the same next step.

phrases.english: There are those who say

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַאי אִיתְחֲזַאי לְהוּ בְּחֶלְמָא,
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai appeared to them in a dream
He said to them:
I have one young bird among you
phrases.notes: He means his son.

phrases.english: and you do not want to bring it to me?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי, רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַאי אִיתְחֲזַאי לְהוּ בְּחֶלְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second version of how the רבנן found out he was unburied
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In this version, his father רבי שמעון בן יוחאי asked in a dream that his son be brought to rest beside him.

steps.title: The people of עכבריא refuse to let him go
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן went to bury him, but the people of עכבריא stopped them. While he lay in the attic, no wild animal had come into their town.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן went to take care of him, but the people of עכבריא did not let them. All the years רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון lay in his attic, no wild beast came into their town.
steps.whatsHappening: The רבנן try to bury him, but the townspeople block them because they feel his presence protects them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This creates a problem the story must solve. The town wanted to keep him because his merit kept wild animals away.

keyTerms.meaning: עכבריא, the town where his body lay

phrases.english: The Rabbis went to take care of his burial
the people of Akhbaria did not let them
because all the years

phrases.aramaic: דַּהֲוָה נָיֵים רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בְּעִילִּיתֵיהּ
phrases.english: that Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon lay in his attic
no wild beast came into their town

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After learning he was unburied, the רבנן try to bury him and run into a problem
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The townspeople refused to let him be buried because his presence protected them from wild animals.

steps.title: On ערב יום כיפור the people of בירי carry him away
steps.stepSummary: On ערב יום כיפור, while the townspeople were busy, the רבנן sent the people of בירי. They took his bier and brought it to his father's cave.
steps.simpleTranslation: One day it was ערב יום כיפור, and they were busy. The רבנן sent word to the people of בירי. They carried out his bier and brought it to his father's cave.
steps.whatsHappening: The רבנן solve the problem by acting on a day when the people of עכבריא were busy preparing for the holiday.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the townspeople were distracted on ערב יום כיפור, they could not block the burial. The people of בירי, from a different town, did the carrying and brought him to his father's burial cave.

keyTerms.meaning: ערב יום כיפור, the day before יום כיפור
His bier (the bed a body is carried on)

phrases.aramaic: יוֹמָא חַד מַעֲלֵי יוֹמָא דְכִיפּוּרֵי הֲוָה,
phrases.english: One day, it was the eve of Yom Kippur
they were busy
phrases.notes: "They" are the people of עכבריא, busy getting ready for the holiday.

phrases.english: The Rabbis sent word to the people of Biri
and they took out his bier
and brought it to his father's cave

steps.triggerLanguage: יוֹמָא חַד מַעֲלֵי יוֹמָא דְכִיפּוּרֵי הֲוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Solves the problem of the townspeople's refusal
steps.mimraCoreRuling: They brought him to his father's cave while the townspeople were busy on ערב יום כיפור.

steps.title: A snake at the cave opens the way for the son
steps.stepSummary: A snake was circling the cave entrance. They asked it to open its mouth so a son could enter next to his father, and it opened for them.
steps.simpleTranslation: They found a snake circling the cave. They said to it: Snake, snake! Open your mouth, and let a son come in next to his father. It opened for them.
steps.whatsHappening: A last obstacle appears at the cave, and it moves aside when they tell it the son is coming to his father. The story ends with him buried beside רבי שמעון בן יוחאי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The snake guarding the cave gives way as soon as it hears this is the son coming to his father. This brings the story full circle back to the dream in step 14, where the father asked for his "young bird."
steps.whatToRemember: רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון was finally buried beside his father רבי שמעון בן יוחאי. Every obstacle gave way: the hidden attic, the town's refusal, and even the snake at the cave.

phrases.english: They found a snake
that was circling the cave
They said to it: Snake, snake!
Open your mouth
and let a son come in next to his father
It opened for them
phrases.notes: The letter in square brackets is added in the corrected wording.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the burial journey begun in the previous step
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The snake opened the way, and the son was buried next to his father.

steps.title: The widow refuses רבי's marriage proposal
steps.stepSummary: רבי proposes to the widow of רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון. She answers that something used by a holy person should not be used by an ordinary one.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי sent someone to propose marriage to his widow. She sent back: Should a vessel used by someone holy now be used by someone ordinary? In ארץ ישראל they say it this way: In the place where the master of the house hangs his sword, should the lowly shepherd hang his basket?
steps.whatsHappening: The story moves on to the widow of רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון. רבי asks to marry her, and she turns him down with a sharp comparison.
steps.deeperAnalysis: She compares herself to a כלי and her late husband to something קודש. Next to him, even רבי counts as חול. The saying 'there they say' gives the same idea in the everyday words people used in ארץ ישראל.

keyTerms.meaning: To propose marriage to his wife (here, the widow)

phrases.english: Rabbi sent someone to propose marriage to his wife,
phrases.notes: 'His wife' means the widow of רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון.

phrases.english: She sent back to him:
A vessel that was used by someone holy,
should it now be used by someone ordinary?
There they say:
phrases.notes: 'There' means ארץ ישראל. This is the same idea in a popular saying.

phrases.english: In the place where the master of the house hangs his sword,
should the lowly shepherd hang his basket?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the burial story ends, the story turns to his widow.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The widow refuses רבי because she sees her late husband as holy compared to him.

steps.title: רבי argues he is greater in good deeds
steps.stepSummary: רבי admits the late scholar was greater in תורה but says he himself is greater in מעשים טובים.
steps.simpleTranslation: He sent back to her: Fine, he was greater than me in תורה. But was he greater than me in good deeds?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי answers the widow. He admits one point but argues another.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי gives up the point about תורה. He tries to win on מעשים טובים instead, which sets up her reply.

phrases.english: He sent back to her:
Granted that in Torah he was greater than me,
but in good deeds,
was he greater than me?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי responds to the widow's refusal.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי grants the late scholar was greater in תורה but claims he himself is greater in good deeds.

steps.title: The widow says he was greater in deeds because he accepted suffering
steps.stepSummary: The widow says she cannot judge תורה, but she knows her husband was greater in deeds because he took יסורים upon himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: She sent back to him: Whether he was greater than you in Torah, I do not know. But in deeds, I do know, because he accepted suffering upon himself.
steps.whatsHappening: The widow turns רבי's argument around. She says that deeds are exactly where her husband was clearly greater.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי said the late scholar was greater only in תורה. She says she cannot judge תורה, but she saw his deeds herself: he willingly accepted יסורים, which the earlier steps described. This closes the exchange and leads into the גמרא's question about תורה.
steps.whatToRemember: The widow refuses רבי because her husband's willingness to accept יסורים made him greater in deeds.

phrases.english: She sent back to him:

phrases.aramaic: בְּתוֹרָה מִיהָא גָּדוֹל מִמְּךָ לָא יָדְעָנָא,
phrases.english: Whether he was greater than you in Torah, I do not know;
in deeds, I do know,
because he accepted suffering upon himself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: She answers רבי's claim about good deeds.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Her late husband was greater in deeds because he accepted suffering.

steps.title: How was he greater in Torah?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what event showed that רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון was greater than רבי in תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: In Torah, what is the story?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to ask a question. רבי admitted the late scholar was greater in תורה, so how was that shown? This sets up the story that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is based on רבי's own words from Step 19. The answer comes in the next steps as a story.

keyTerms.meaning: What is it? What is the story?

phrases.english: In Torah, what is the story?
phrases.notes: This points back to רבי's words in Step 19, 'he was greater than me in Torah.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Picks up רבי's admission about תורה and asks for the event behind it.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What showed that רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון was greater than רבי in Torah?

steps.title: The two young scholars sat on the ground before the great Sages
steps.stepSummary: The answer begins: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל and רבי יהושע בן קרחה sat on benches, and the two young scholars sat on the ground in front of them.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבן שמעון בן גמליאל and רבי יהושע בן קרחה sat on benches, רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון and רבי sat on the ground in front of them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts answering with a story. First it sets the scene of who sat where.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sitting on benches showed senior status. The two young scholars sat on the floor out of respect. This seating is what changes in the next steps.

phrases.aramaic: דְּכִי הֲווֹ יָתְבִי רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
phrases.english: When Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel
and Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korcha were sitting on benches,

phrases.aramaic: יָתְבִי קַמַּיְיהוּ רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
phrases.english: there would sit before them Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon
and Rabbi, on the ground.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּכִי הֲווֹ יָתְבִי רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the question of Step 21.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A story about the seating of the young scholars in the בית מדרש.

steps.title: The young scholars are raised to benches
steps.stepSummary: The two young scholars asked and answered brilliantly, so the חכמים gave them benches and raised them up.
steps.simpleTranslation: They would ask questions and answer them. The Sages said: We are drinking from their waters, and they sit on the ground? So they made benches for them and raised them up.
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues. The two young scholars were so sharp that the חכמים promoted them to sit on benches.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Drinking from their waters' means learning from them. The חכמים felt it was wrong for their own teachers to sit on the floor.

keyTerms.meaning: They raised questions and answered them
We drink from their waters (we learn from them)

phrases.english: They would ask questions and answer them.
The Sages said:
We are drinking from their waters,
phrases.notes: They mean: we are learning תורה from them.

phrases.english: and they are sitting on the ground?!
They made benches for them and raised them up.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story and changes the seating.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Both young scholars were brilliant enough to be promoted to benches.

steps.title: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל has his son lowered
steps.stepSummary: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל objects that promoting his only son puts him in danger, so they lower רבי back to the ground.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל said to them: I have one little bird among you, and you want to make me lose it? They lowered רבי.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי's father objects to his son's promotion. The חכמים lower רבי back down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'little bird' is his son רבי. He fears that such early honor could harm him. Now only רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון is left on a bench, which sets up the next objection.

keyTerms.meaning: To make it lost, to destroy it

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לָהֶן רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל:
phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel said to them:
I have one little bird among you,
phrases.notes: The little bird is his son, רבי.

phrases.english: and you want to make me lose it?
They lowered Rabbi.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reverses the promotion for רבי only.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי is lowered at his father's request.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון is lowered too and feels insulted
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן קרחה argues that the fatherless scholar deserves the same protection, so he is lowered too. He is hurt, feeling he was treated as equal to רבי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן קרחה said to them: Should the one who has a father live, and the one with no father die? So they lowered רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון too. He was hurt and said: You consider him equal to me?
steps.whatsHappening: The second young scholar is lowered for the same protective reason. He takes it as an insult, and this shows he saw himself as greater than רבי in תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע בן קרחה points out that רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון has no father to protect him, so he needs the same care. Nobody tells him the reason, so he thinks he is being ranked equal with רבי. His complaint answers Step 21: he was the greater one in תורה.
steps.whatToRemember: The seating story shows רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון was greater than רבי in תורה. That is why he felt insulted at being treated as equal to him.
steps.confusionAlert: He was not lowered because the חכמים thought less of him. They lowered him to protect him, but he did not know that.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לָהֶן רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן קׇרְחָה:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korcha said to them:
Should the one who has a father live,
and the one who has no father die?

phrases.aramaic: אֲחֲתוּהּ נָמֵי לְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן.
phrases.english: So they also lowered Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon.
He was hurt,
and said: You consider him equal to me?
phrases.notes: 'Him' is רבי. Lowering them together made it look like they were equals.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the demotion to the second scholar and shows his reaction.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: His offense at being equated with רבי shows his greater stature in Torah.

steps.title: Before that day, he used to support רבי
steps.stepSummary: Until the bench incident, whenever רבי said something in תורה, רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון would back him up.
steps.simpleTranslation: Until that day, whenever רבי said a teaching, רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון would support him.
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues, describing how things were between the two scholars before the bench incident. This sets up the change coming in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now, רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון played a helping role and supported רבי's ideas. Spelling out the 'before' lets us see clearly how much changed afterward.

phrases.english: Until that day,
phrases.notes: 'That day' is the day the two of them were lowered from the benches.

phrases.english: when רבי would say a matter,

phrases.aramaic: הֲוָה מְסַיַּיע לֵיהּ רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן:
phrases.english: רבי אלעזר son of רבי שמעון would support him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story after רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון was hurt at being lowered along with רבי.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Before the incident, he supported רבי's statements.

steps.title: From then on, he got ahead of רבי's objections and dismissed them
steps.stepSummary: After the incident, when רבי said 'I have an objection,' רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון would say the objection before him and call it empty.
steps.simpleTranslation: From then on, whenever רבי said 'I have something to answer,' רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון told him: 'This and this is what you want to say. That is your answer. Now you have just loaded us down with bundles of answers that have no substance.'
steps.whatsHappening: The story shows the change. רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון now guesses רבי's objection ahead of time and brushes it off as worthless.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the real proof for the question in step 21. He could predict exactly what רבי was going to say and show it was weak, which means he was the sharper scholar.

keyTerms.meaning: I have an answer or objection to raise

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the main evidence that answers step 21's question about how רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון was greater in תורה.

phrases.english: From here on,

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הֲוָה אָמַר רַבִּי ״יֵשׁ לִי לְהָשִׁיב״,
phrases.english: when רבי would say, "I have something to respond,"

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן:
phrases.english: רבי אלעזר son of רבי שמעון would say to him:
Such and such is what you have to respond,
this is your answer.
Now you have surrounded us
phrases.notes: He's teasing רבי: 'Your objection just forced us to pile up answers for nothing.'

phrases.english: with bundles of answers that have no substance.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasts with step 26: he goes from supporting רבי to getting ahead of and dismissing him.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: His ability to predict and dismiss רבי's objections shows he was greater in תורה.

steps.title: רבי is hurt, and his father comforts him
steps.stepSummary: רבי feels bad and tells his father. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says the other scholar is a lion son of a lion, while רבי is a lion son of a fox.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי felt hurt. He went and told his father. His father said: 'My son, don't feel bad. He is a lion son of a lion, and you are a lion son of a fox.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי complains to his father. His father explains why the other scholar is stronger: he had a greater father, רבי שמעון בר יוחאי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל admits that רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון really is greater, which confirms the answer to step 21. He also humbly calls himself a 'fox' compared to רבי שמעון, and this sets up the next step about humble people.
steps.whatToRemember: The story's point is now complete: רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון was greater in תורה, and even רבי's own father admits it.

phrases.english: רבי felt hurt.
He came and told his father.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: בְּנֵי, אַל יֵרַע לָךְ,
phrases.english: He said to him: My son, do not feel bad,
for he is a lion son of a lion,
and you are a lion son of a fox.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows רבי's reaction to being dismissed in step 27 and his father's explanation.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Even רבן שמעון בן גמליאל agrees that רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון is greater, because of his great father.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון was greater than רבי in תורה.

steps.title: רבי's teaching that there are three humble people, starting with his father
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא connects the father's humble words to רבי's teaching that there are three humble people. The first one listed is 'Father.'
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what רבי meant when he said: 'There are three humble people, and they are: Father...'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא links the story to a well-known statement of רבי and begins listing the three humble people. The rest of the list continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל called himself a 'fox' even though he was the נשיא. That humility explains why רבי counts his father among the three humble people.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what [he] meant when he said

phrases.english: This is what רבי said:
There are three humble people,
and they are: Father,
phrases.notes: 'Father' is רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, the one who just called himself a fox.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the father's humble words in step 28 as the background for רבי's statement.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי teaches that there are three humble people, and the first is his father, רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
